subject: octopus
title: Octopuses Throw Things at Each Other, and Females Do Most of It

scenes.text: Octopuses throw things at each other. Females throw the most.
In Jervis Bay, Australia, cameras recorded 24 hours of gloomy octopuses living side by side.
They counted 102 throws. An octopus gathers silt or shells in its arms and fires it with a jet of water.
Two thirds of the throws came from females. About one in six hit another octopus.
One female kept pelting a male who was trying to mate with her. He kept ducking.
And nobody who got hit ever threw back.

description:
Wild octopuses have been filmed throwing silt, shells and algae, sometimes straight at each other.
Researchers led by Peter Godfrey-Smith analyzed 24 hours of video of gloomy octopuses (Octopus tetricus) in Jervis Bay, Australia, recorded in 2015 and 2016, and counted 102 throws by roughly 10 animals. The octopus holds material in its arms and blasts it away with a jet from its siphon, often several body lengths. About 66 percent of throws were by females, about half happened during interactions with other octopuses, and about 17 percent hit one. The study, published in PLOS ONE in 2022, is the first report of throwing in octopuses; the authors say only that some throws appear to be targeted.
Who would win a throwing contest, you or an octopus? Comment below.
first_comment: Darker octopuses threw harder and were more likely to hit, and twice the debris struck a passing fish. What would you throw back?
